target.policy: Clean-room classification from public documentation, black-box oracle output, and OpenRSCAD's public implementation/tests; verified does not imply exhaustive input coverage.

features.summary: Assignments, last-write-wins hoisting, dead RHS suppression, and no-forward-reference behavior match the oracle cases.
Conditional expressions and nesting are oracle-covered.
User module definition, lexical lookup, and invocation are exercised through observable echoes.
Named functions, recursion, mutual recursion, and calls are oracle-covered.
Function literals and calls through function values are oracle-covered.
Positional and named binding, including named-after-positional and defaulted parameters, match the oracle.

A $-prefixed argument is dynamically scoped over the callee and everything under it, for builtin modules, user modules and their children(), and function calls; each argument expression evaluates once in the caller's scope and does not leak past the call.

Omitted function and module defaults are lazy and use the definition's ordinary lexical environment, while special variables remain dynamic and explicit arguments use caller scope; these paths are oracle-covered.
Ordinary bindings and closures use lexical scope.
Special variables follow the dynamic call chain.
Statement-level if/else, including else-if chains and non-boolean conditions, matches the oracle.
Statement-level for over ranges, stepped ranges, lists, and multiple (cartesian) generators matches the oracle.

A bare `{ ... }` block groups statements and scopes its assignments, matching the oracle.
Expression-prefix echo returns its body and preserves side-effect order.

The `*` disable modifier removes a subtree from the render, matching the oracle.
The `!` root modifier renders its subtree alone, matching the oracle.
The `#` highlight modifier is preview-only and leaves the rendered mesh unchanged, matching the oracle.
The `%` background modifier excludes a subtree from the render, matching the oracle.
Line and block comments, including comment-like text inside strings, match the oracle.
Dependent Cartesian bindings produce one intersected operand per iteration.
Scoped bindings whose right-hand sides all evaluate in the enclosing scope and take effect together, unlike let(); bindings do not escape the body.
Undefined propagation, comparison, indexing, and iteration cases are oracle-covered.

OpenRSCAD-only range predicate, exercised by the BOSL2 gate. OpenSCAD has no such function and returns undef, so an oracle case would pin the divergence rather than the behaviour; the extension tier keeps it out of the OpenSCAD exit criterion.
Range, reproducibility, and global/seeded advancement semantics are implemented, but the xorshift sequence is not bit-compatible with OpenSCAD.
features.rationale: OpenRSCAD intentionally uses a deterministic xorshift generator; identical upstream pseudo-random values are not promised.

features.summary: `version()` and `version_num()` report the declared compatibility baseline 2021.01 as [2021, 1, 0] / 20210100; upstream reports whichever OpenSCAD build is running.
features.rationale: An engine reports its own version. OpenRSCAD states the OpenSCAD baseline it targets rather than impersonating a specific upstream build, so no oracle value can be matched and a version-gated script may take a different branch.

A zero or negative component yields no geometry, matching upstream.
Radius and explicit/adaptive fragment controls have geometry oracles.
`sphere(d=)` matches the oracle and takes precedence over `r`.
Cylinders, cones, centering, the fourth positional center argument, and explicit fragment counts are geometry-oracle covered.
`cylinder(d=)`, `d1=`, and `d2=` match the oracle and take precedence over the radii.
Non-positive height, a negative radius, or two zero radii yield no geometry; a single zero radius remains a valid cone.
Indexed triangular faces have a committed geometry oracle.
Faces wind clockwise seen from outside; an inside-out but consistently wound solid is a positive solid to the CSG kernel, so it adds under union and cuts under difference, matching the oracle.
`convexity=` is accepted as a preview hint and does not change the mesh, matching the oracle.
Planar concave faces use projected earcut triangulation; a boolean-sensitive U-prism regression has a committed OpenSCAD geometry oracle.
The deprecated `triangles=` alias for `faces=` matches the oracle.
Positive scalar/vector sizes and centering have extrusion-based geometry oracles.
A zero or negative component yields no geometry, matching upstream.

A zero or negative radius yields no geometry.

`circle(d=)` matches the oracle and takes precedence over `r`.
Single paths and explicit outer/hole paths have extrusion-based geometry oracles.
`convexity=` is accepted as a preview hint and does not change the mesh, matching the oracle.
Bundled Liberation Sans/Serif/Mono family and style outlines have geometry oracles.
halign uses the advance width; valign aligns the ink box, not the font ascender/descender, so x-height-only text sits differently from text with ascenders.

features.surface: text() kerning, ligatures, and complex-script shaping
features.summary: Runs are shaped with rustybuzz, the Rust port of the HarfBuzz shaper OpenSCAD uses, so kerning pairs, ligatures and joining scripts match rather than being summed glyph by glyph.
direction selects ltr/rtl/ttb/btt and script/language are passed to the shaper; a vertical run centres each glyph in an OS/2 typographic ascent-to-descent slot and on the column, as upstream.

features.surface: textmetrics(text, size, font, halign, valign, spacing, direction, language, script)
features.summary: Returns an object with position, size, ascent, descent, offset, and advance for a text run, shaped with the same rustybuzz path as text(). The ink box is derived from exact glyph extents, so it matches the oracle to <0.01mm; OpenSCAD's FreeType fixed-point outline scaling is not replicated (documented in COMPAT.md).
features.notes: Experimental in OpenSCAD (requires --enable=textmetrics). Field values and alignment behaviour are covered by crates/openrscad-eval/tests/textmetrics.rs against the 2024.12 oracle.

features.summary: Returns an object with nominal (hhea) and max (glyph-bbox) ascent/descent, interline advance, and the resolved font family/style. Values are a straight scaling of the face's tables and match the oracle to <1e-3.
features.notes: Experimental in OpenSCAD (requires --enable=textmetrics).

features.summary: The ObjectType value returned by textmetrics()/fontmetrics(): an ordered key->value map read with .field or ["field"], echoed as `{ key = value; ... }`. Cannot be constructed in source, matching upstream.
features.notes: Introduced to carry textmetrics/fontmetrics results; see COMPAT.md.

features.summary: Explicit height, centering, twist, scale, and slices have geometry oracles.
`convexity=` is accepted as a preview hint and does not change the mesh, matching the oracle.
segments= subdivides each profile outline, applies without twist, and overrides $fn/$fa/$fs.
An omitted slice count takes the tighter of the $fa per-slice twist limit and the $fs helical-travel limit, or $fn slices per revolution.
A twisted profile outline is re-tessellated from $fn/$fa/$fs independently of the slice count, apportioning a per-contour segment budget across edges by length.

Combined twist and non-uniform scale now match the oracle. Each edge is refined by the peak stretch its direction reaches over the swept slices (max_t |diag(sx(t),sy(t))·Rot(t·twist)·d|), which subsumes the pure-twist own-length and pure-scale max(original,scaled) rules, and the layer sweep rotates then scales in the fixed frame. The headline case moved from +0.77% (956 tris) to exact (246.445, 1244 tris).

features.surface: roof() straight-skeleton roof of a 2D profile
features.summary: A convex profile is lifted to its straight skeleton exactly (volume, bounds, and centroid match the oracle for squares, rectangles, triangles, and regular polygons). A concave profile or one with holes needs split events and is warned and skipped rather than mis-roofed. Experimental upstream (--enable=roof).

A non-planar wall quad is split along its shorter diagonal, ties falling back to the wall lean (twist direction, flipped for a hole). Matched per quad against the oracle over 3142 quads, and exact for off-axis, holed, and non-uniformly scaled curved profiles.

A non-uniform scale refines the profile by max(original, scaled) edge length and adds slices from the worst point travel; a uniform scale keeps the walls planar and refines nothing. Triangle counts are pinned, not just volume.
A non-positive height yields no geometry; the children are still evaluated so their echo/assert side effects run.
Post-baseline oblique extrusion along a normalized direction has committed geometry oracles.
Full/partial sweeps, negative-side profiles, over-rotation, axis crossings, and partial fragment counts have geometry oracles.
`convexity=` is accepted as a preview hint and does not change the mesh, matching the oracle.

features.summary: 2D sums, convex 3D sums, and distribution over explicit unions have geometry oracles.

features.surface: minkowski() with a genuinely concave 3D leaf
features.summary: A concave leaf is replaced by its convex hull, with a runtime warning; explicit unions of convex parts remain exact.
`render(convexity=)` forces an exact sub-render and yields the same geometry as the subtree, matching the oracle.
`group()` unions its children like a bare block, matching the oracle.
Named/scalar/list/string formatting and child pass-through are exercised throughout the echo oracle suite.
A passing `assert()` yields its children unchanged, with or without a message, matching the oracle.
`children()` bare, by index, by index list, and by range all match the oracle.
Singular child selection; bare child() is the first child alone, where bare children() is all of them.
Included definitions, assignments, and side effects have an echo oracle.

features.surface: include/use paths with spaces and punctuation
features.summary: Include/use paths are taken raw to the closing bracket, preserving spaces and punctuation, matching the oracle.
A relative include resolves against the including file's own directory, not the caller's or the process cwd, matching the oracle.
A library not found beside the script is resolved from OPENSCADPATH, matching the oracle run with the same directory on its environment.
Representative STL mesh import has a geometry oracle.
Representative OFF mesh import has a geometry oracle.
AMF import matches the oracle, including multiple `<volume>`s sharing one object's vertex list.
A representative compressed 3MF mesh has a geometry oracle.
`convexity=` is accepted as a preview hint and does not change the imported mesh, matching the oracle.
OBJ import matches the oracle, including 1-based indices and quad faces.
A representative simple 2D DXF import has an extrusion-based geometry oracle.
Keeps only entities on the named layer; a selector matching nothing yields no geometry.
Places the imported outline as (point - origin) * scale; both are 2D-only, as upstream, and do not affect a mesh import.

features.surface: DXF curve entities and caller fragment controls
features.summary: LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/ELLIPSE/LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE import, tessellated by the call-site $fn/$fa/$fs. Bulges (group 42) and SPLINE are deliberately not expanded: OpenSCAD 2024.12 imports neither, so expanding them would be a divergence.
A representative basic SVG path import has an extrusion-based geometry oracle.
layer= selects an Inkscape layer group by label and id= selects any element by id; either keeps that subtree alone.

features.surface: SVG transforms, dimensions, units, and DPI options
features.summary: translate/scale/rotate/matrix/skew transforms compose down the tree and with an element own transform; a physical width pins the scale, else viewBox units are inches at dpi (default 72), and with no viewBox coordinates are 1:1.

features.surface: SVG nesting, use, style, and visibility
features.summary: The document is walked as a tree: <use> instantiates a referenced element, <defs> draws nothing, display:none hides (attribute or style) while visibility:hidden does not, and an explicit id= overrides display:none but not <defs>.

features.surface: AMF/3MF units, objects, components, and build transforms
features.summary: 3MF `<build>` items are assembled with their transforms and repeat instancing; upstream ignores `<build>` and imports only the highest-id object. AMF `unit` and `<constellation>` are ignored by both.
features.notes: Multi-object 3MF cannot have a geom oracle case because we deliberately differ there; covered by unit tests in crates/openrscad-geom/src/mesh.rs and documented in COMPAT.md.
features.rationale: Silently discarding a user's geometry is the worse failure, and OpenRSCAD's own colour-group 3MF export writes one object per colour, which upstream's rule would make unreadable. Single-object packages are identical either way.

features.summary: A plain alias for import(): the format still comes from the file suffix, not the module name.
A plain alias for import(): the format still comes from the file suffix, not the module name.

Reads a DIMENSION measurement, matching on the dimension text and recomputing from the definition points; linear dimensions project onto the group-50 rotation, aligned ones use the plain distance, radius and diameter the centre-to-chord distance.
Returns the intersection of two lines on a layer, mapped through (point - origin) * scale; an empty layer selector matches any layer.
Whitespace heightmaps have a committed geometry oracle.
`center`, `invert`, and `convexity` on a `.dat` heightfield match the oracle (upstream ignores `invert` outside PNG).
PNG heightfields match the oracle, including upstream's `invert`, which offsets the relief by inverting the sample against 1 rather than 255.

Kernel-aware contour export is wired across first-party hosts; 2D output bytes are not yet upstream-oracle gated. Export formats have no `.scad`-level oracle: the comparison would be byte identity, which is outside the compatibility contract.

Raster rendering, camera, projection, and image sizing are implemented; GUI/raster pixel parity is outside the core language criterion. Export formats have no `.scad`-level oracle: the comparison would be byte identity, which is outside the compatibility contract.

Serializes the evaluated tree as OpenSCAD .csg -- every module resolved, every transform lowered to multmatrix. Round-trip tested: re-rendering the output reproduces the geometry in both engines. Text is not byte-identical because OpenSCAD omits defaulted parameters and the IR does not record which were written. Export formats have no `.scad`-level oracle: the comparison would be byte identity, which is outside the compatibility contract.
features.notes: Like every other export entry this has no .scad-level oracle case, so it stays implemented rather than verified; covered by crates/openrscad-cli/tests/csg_roundtrip.rs.

features.summary: An unrecognized or missing -o suffix is rejected before any render, exiting non-zero and writing nothing, matching the 2024.12 binary across eleven suffixes; recognized suffixes match case-insensitively. Unit-tested, but like every other export entry it has no .scad-level oracle case, so it stays implemented rather than verified. Export formats have no `.scad`-level oracle: the comparison would be byte identity, which is outside the compatibility contract.
